components.description: Paid parental leave for an employee on an Academic Year appointment who becomes a biological parent or has a child placed pending adoption: full pay in the Fall or Spring semester (.33 FTE in Summer A or B), up to 26 consecutive weeks, once per career at FIU (BOT-UFF Policy on Leaves s.7(a), (c)).
components.faculty_group_note: "an employee on an Academic Year appointment" in the UFF bargaining unit (Professor, Associate Professor, Assistant Professor and other titles; College of Law and College of Medicine employees are outside the unit). Academic Year appointment is the standard faculty appointment.
components.eligible_parent_wording: "becomes a biological parent or a child is placed in the employee's home pending adoption"; foster care is not covered ("Foster care is not covered under parental leave"), so foster is not listed
components.entitlement_note: "at the employee's request, shall be granted": the University must grant it once requested; the employee chooses timing within the window (V2, schema: 'shall be granted upon request').

components.relief_note: Formal leave of absence; relief not stated (R9).
components.time_window: shall begin no earlier than the first day of classes in the semester during which the child's birth or placement is expected or occurs, whichever is earlier, and shall end no later than one year from the date of the birth or placement
components.use_limit_note: "once during his or her employment career at FIU" (s.7(c)); s.7(f): once per career the 26 weeks may be split into two intervals for two births, never used in more than two semesters in the career.
components.return_obligation: may be required, at the discretion of the University, to return to employment at FIU for two (2) semesters (nine-month contract); otherwise the University may recoup the value of the parental leave
components.notice: written request not less than 120 days before a leave of one semester or more, if practicable (Policy on Leaves s.1(a))

components.institution_label: Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) Entitlements
components.description: Federal FMLA leave as implemented by Policy on Leaves s.6: 480 hours (12 workweeks) of job-protected leave without pay in a rolling 12 months for birth, adoption or foster placement, the employee's serious health condition or care of a family member. For parental leave it is counted only against leave beyond the paid parental leave (s.6(b)(2)).
components.faculty_group_note: "An employee, whether salaried or paid from Other Personal Services (OPS)" who is FMLA-eligible
components.eligible_parent_wording: "a birth or placement for adoption or foster care"; statute: "birth of a son or daughter of the employee"
components.entitlement_note: Statutory entitlement; "The University shall approve FMLA leave for an eligible employee".
components.duration_note: Policy: "up to four hundred and eighty (480) hours" (= 12 workweeks at 40 hours); statute: "a total of 12 workweeks". Coded at the statute's 12 workweeks with the policy's qualifier "up to" (R13); the policy restates the statute without adding length. The University "may require" use of accrued paid leave before leave without pay (s.6(d)(2)); not a must-exhaust requirement as written.

notes: Governing document on 2018-02-22: the FIU BOT-UFF Collective Bargaining Agreement 2015-2018 as ratified 2017-03-24, Appendix G BOT-UFF Policies (Policy on Leaves ss.1-12). Appendix G says the Policies are 'binding upon the parties' though 'not made a part of' the Agreement for grievance purposes. Tenure-stream faculty are in the unit (Appendix A: Professor, Associate Professor, Assistant Professor); College of Law and College of Medicine employees are excluded, which leaves arts and sciences and engineering covered (V3).

2018_00_link (2019 Wayback capture of the Faculty Careers page) quotes the parental leave policy with wording not in the 2015-2018 agreement ('the employee or employee's same-sex domestic partner becomes a biological parent'); it post-dates the reference date and is a summary, so the agreement's wording is coded and the page is cited only in the passage accounting.

2018_03 is a summary of the AY2016-17 amendments (Art. 3.4(g), Art. 11 salaries, Appendix A, promotions policy); it changes no leave terms. 2018_04: only the December 5, 2016 memo was used; the December 7, 2018 addendum (26 weeks of paid leave; working while on leave) post-dates 2018-02-22 and was ignored.

Whom the figures describe (U8): an Academic Year (nine-month) appointee, the standard faculty appointment; s.7(c) is coded for that member as c1. The 12-month appointee's paid leave (s.7(b)) is recorded as c2 under its own group name and is not linked to c1 (different groups, not alternatives).

Birth parent chain: paid parental leave up to 26 weeks (c1, full pay in Fall/Spring, .33 FTE in Summer) -> parental leave without pay up to 1 year (c3), with FMLA 12 workweeks (c6) from its start and further accrued leave (c5, own balance) usable after c1; pregnancy-related illness may be paid from accrued sick leave (c4, own balance, unplaced).

Non-birth parent chain: paid parental leave up to 26 weeks (c1) -> parental leave without pay up to 1 year (c3), with FMLA 12 workweeks (c6) from its start; further accrued leave (c5) after c1; sick leave to care for the birth parent (c10, own balance, unplaced).

FMLA placement: Policy on Leaves s.6(b)(2) counts FMLA only against parental leave that 'extends beyond the period of paid parental leave', so FMLA is linked consecutive_after the paid leave (S1 exception, the institution's own text) and concurrent_with the unpaid extension. The statutory floor is filled from statutory_baseline.csv (U7).

Calendar: Art. 19 defines 'Semester' as 'one of the two approximately 19.5 week periods which together constitute the academic year' of 'approximately 39 contiguous weeks'; this is the appointment period (as Wisconsin's 19.5-week pay semester in R8), not the teaching term, so calendar.kind = semester, and the term length follows R8's order. No component is measured in semesters.

Not components: sabbaticals and professional development leave (research purposes; professional development leave excludes tenure-stream), bereavement, jury, military, disaster and athletic leaves, workers' compensation leave, phased-retirement participants' leave, tuition waivers, and the dependent-care flexible spending account (pre-tax benefits) - none is a leave or pay a parent could take for a birth (checklist s.1).

Cross-references not saved: the sick leave pool's terms (s.8(a)(2)a); the FMLA regulations, 29 CFR Part 825 (s.6(h)); 'FIU policies regarding dependent care and medical leave' named generically in the 2016 memo (no separate policy named).
No leave_limits entry: s.6(b)(2) 'up to six (6) months' restates the 26-week paid leave, and s.7(d) allows paid, accrued and unpaid leave in combination with no stated total. No all-sources pay cap.
The pay level of c1 is full pay in the Fall and Spring semesters and .33 FTE in Summer A or B; for an academic-year appointee the summer pay is not part of the regular appointment.
